AgentEvidenceCode.description:
Optional agent evidence that was dropped so the mandatory report is kept.

An agent report carries a mandatory core (identity, lease, capacity, outcome)
and optional evidence (NICs, the NAS route, fabric details, readings,
progress, diagnostics). Invalid optional evidence is never a reason to refuse
the core: the evidence is dropped and one of these words names what was lost,
on the agent that dropped it and on the Controller that received it.

ResourceBlockerCode.description:
The capacity-fit codes the resource planner gives a node that cannot fit.

``insufficient`` is the family prefix a run admission maps onto
``run.insufficient_memory``; the planner itself names the exact
``insufficient_capacity*`` member.  Those are waits: a claim, a stop or a
fresh inventory can free the memory.  ``demand_exceeds_capacity`` is not in
that family: nothing the platform holds or plans to release can make the
demand fit the Spark (or one load's own assignments fit beside each other),
so the same request fails the same way and ends on its first occurrence.
``insufficient_swap`` is a wait too: the load phase's rise above the
steady demand needs more usable swap than the Spark has free now (another
load still starting holds it, or the swap setting is too small).
ResourceBlockerCode.title: ResourceBlockerCode

RunAdmissionCode.description:
The typed codes a run admission names for a refusal, blocker or wait.

``capacity_busy`` is lock contention only.  Every other reason an admission
must wait or is refused carries its own member, so a waiting operation shows
the real cause.  The retryable blockers (a plan that may become admissible
by itself) are a subset the Controller derives from these members.
RunAdmissionCode.title: RunAdmissionCode

checks of Run/Switch.  ``failure_classification`` derives its code set from
this enum, so the Controller and the contract cannot disagree.
